cells.tense: You're on that threshold right now, holding everything you've gathered, and you get to decide what gets offered up and what gets let go.
cells.ask: When the next possibility pulls, take one clear look at what the pattern actually shows and let that — not the pull — tell you which way to step.
cells.core:
You've pulled together what this thing was going to be, and you can feel the moment has arrived to hand it off. The feelings you gathered along the way were real; you stayed with them long enough to find out what they had to say. When the next one tugs at you, you'll have both the want and the read on it. What you carry forward is something you can see the shape of.

One more possibility will always show up and ask to be wanted. The thing that makes this hold is looking at a pattern long enough to understand it, then acting from that instead of from the ache. Choosing well is what this moment is for.
cells.sheetLine: You've gathered it, you can read it, and you're free to choose what goes forward.

cells.tense: You're already out past the moment you're in, feeling what every possibility might turn into before any of it has actually happened.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been holding together for dear life and let it be finished — not abandoned, just done.
cells.core:
There are so many ways this could feel, and you're feeling all of them ahead of time — which one they'll pick, how it'll land, what it says about you. That's not the moment, that's a rehearsal happening in your head. The endings you keep postponing are the ones that would let the real thing begin.

A completed thing doesn't need you gripping it anymore. What it needs is for you to believe the ending was right and the next part is real. That trust is what's missing when you hold on, and it's what comes back when you do less.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing against a future that hasn't happened instead of letting what's finished be finished.

cells.tense: You were standing at a moment that belonged to you, and you've stayed behind it — still there, while the present moves on.
cells.ask: Let your mind settle into one thing long enough to actually see it, and trust that this alone can carry you back to the present.
cells.core:
The door is already behind you and you're still at it, waiting for something to tell you it's okay to walk through. There's no lack of wanting in you; what's starved is the quiet that lets you hold two or three possibilities in your head at once and stay in contact with all of them. You can still get it back.

One thing, looked at long enough to understand it, will do more for you than ten things half-seen. The stillness isn't a retreat — it's what brings you back into the room. When your mind is at rest, the moment stops moving past you.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at a moment the present has moved past.

cells.tense: You're pulling feelings and possibilities toward this thing right now — deciding what it should feel like, gathering what it could mean — and you're describing all of it as just what's happening.
cells.ask: Find the pattern underneath one thing and say out loud that the reading came from you.
cells.core:
At this doorstep you know which feeling in the room is yours and which belongs to someone else. You sort through what's possible, keep what's real, and can say what you noticed without needing anyone to confirm it. The picking has your name on it and everyone can feel that.

Right now every possibility that's gathered around this thing is being chosen — by how you hold it, what you call it, which feeling you give the most room to. That choosing is yours, and you keep talking like the thing is doing it on its own. Seeing one pattern clearly is the simplest form of the same act, and it's the one you've been stepping around.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping what this feels like and talking like the feeling is shaping you.
